answer_text:
# 🦴 Calcium-Containing Foods

Calcium is the most abundant mineral in your body and a major component of your bones and teeth. Since your body can't make calcium on its own, it's essential to consume calcium-rich foods to meet your daily needs.

Calcium is used for numerous functions, including building bones and teeth, muscle contraction, blood clotting, maintenance of cell membranes, and nerve transmission.

---

## 🥛 Dairy Products (Highest Sources)

Dairy products such as milk, cheese, and yogurt are the most concentrated food sources of calcium — for example, one cup of milk contains approximately 271 mg of calcium.

| Food | Calcium Content |
|------|----------------|
| **Parmesan Cheese** | 242 mg per oz (28g) |
| **Plain Yogurt (whole milk)** | ~206 mg per 6 oz |
| **Milk** | ~271 mg per cup |
| **Swiss Cheese** | Very high |

Yogurt is an excellent source of calcium, and many types are also rich in probiotics — a type of beneficial bacteria that can promote immune function, improve heart health, and enhance nutrient absorption.

Most cheeses are excellent sources of calcium. Parmesan cheese has the most, with 242 mg — or 24% of the daily value — per ounce (28 grams). Softer cheeses tend to have less.

---

## 🐟 Fish & Seafood

Sardines and canned salmon are loaded with calcium, thanks to their edible bones. Canned pink salmon provides about 241 mg per 3 oz serving.

---

## 🌿 Plant-Based Sources

Many plant foods are also calcium-rich, including greens, beans, tofu, nuts, and seeds.

| Food | Notes |
|------|-------|
| **Tofu** | Most concentrated non-dairy source |
| **Kale & Bok Choy** | Good absorption |
| **Broccoli** | Good absorption |
| **Beans (Black, White)** | ~239 mg per cup (black beans) |
| **Turnip Greens** | ~209 mg per cup |
| **Chia & Sesame Seeds** | High in calcium |
| **Almonds** | Good plant source |

Seeds are tiny nutritional powerhouses, and many are high in calcium, including poppy, sesame, celery, and chia seeds.

Tofu is the most concentrated source of non-dairy calcium.

---

## 🥣 Fortified Foods

Fortified foods like cereals can make it easier to meet your daily calcium needs. You can also find a variety of plant-based beverages, such as plant milks and orange juice, that have been fortified with calcium.

---

## ⚠️ Absorption Tips

Vitamin D is required for calcium to be absorbed in the gut and to maintain adequate calcium levels in the blood.

Some healthy foods also contain compounds like insoluble fiber and oxalic acid that bind with calcium and hinder its absorption. For example, greens like spinach and chard are higher in oxalic acid, but others like kale, collard greens, and bok choy contain lower amounts, so the calcium they contain is better absorbed.

Recommended Dietary Allowances for calcium range from **1,000 to 1,200 mg for adults** and from 200 to 1,300 mg for infants, children, and adolescents, depending on age.

---

> 💡 **Tip:** Try to choose a wide variety of foods from the different food groups so your bones can get all the nutrients they need.
